issues.legal_issue: A co-heir’s possession becomes adverse to another co-heir only when the required ouster is established.
material_facts: The parties were found to be agnatic relations of the same degree and co-heirs of the deceased owner.
One co-heir obtained possession after suing alone on a claim of exclusive title, and he alone enjoyed the properties and their profits.
The other co-heir did not participate in the earlier suit and remained silent about his asserted right.
The court considered that the circumstances might support an inference of ouster, but declined to decide the appeal on that ground.
issues.conclusion: A co-heir’s possession is ordinarily treated as possession for all co-heirs. To establish adverse possession against another co-heir, the claimant must prove an open assertion of hostile title together with exclusive possession and enjoyment to the other co-heir’s knowledge. The court did not decide whether ouster was established on these facts.
issues.legal_principle: Possession by one co-heir is presumed to rest on the joint title and does not become adverse merely because that co-heir has sole possession or a secret hostile intention. Ouster requires an open assertion of hostile title and exclusive possession and enjoyment to the knowledge of the excluded co-heir; the burden rests on the person claiming to displace the co-heir’s title. The court relied on Corea v. Appuhamy, N. Varada Pillai v. Jeevarathnammal, Culley v. Deod Taylerson, and Govindrao v. Rajabai.

rule.if: coheir_adverse_possession_claim and hostile_title_openly_asserted and exclusive_possession_and_enjoyment and other_coheir_knew

predicates.coheir_adverse_possession_claim: A person claiming adverse possession seeks to defeat another person’s title as a co-heir.
predicates.hostile_title_openly_asserted: The co-heir in possession openly asserted a title hostile to the other co-heir’s title.
predicates.exclusive_possession_and_enjoyment: The co-heir in possession held and enjoyed the property exclusively.
predicates.other_coheir_knew: The other co-heir knew of the hostile assertion and exclusive possession and enjoyment.

issues.definition: When a co-heir in possession openly asserts hostile title and exclusively possesses and enjoys the property to the other co-heir’s knowledge, ouster is established.

issues.legal_issue: Possession by a court-appointed receiver cannot be tacked to the later adverse possession of a person who was initially out of possession.
material_facts: A receiver was appointed to possess the properties while a suit against third-party possessors was pending.
The person who later obtained the properties had not been in possession before the receiver took possession.
After the suit was decreed, that person obtained actual possession from the receiver.
The receiver was an officer of the court, not an agent of the successful party, and the co-heirs out of possession could not sue for possession while the receiver held the properties.
issues.conclusion: The receiver’s period of possession could not be added to the later possessor’s period of adverse possession. Adverse possession, if any, could begin only when the later possessor obtained actual possession with the requisite hostile claim.
issues.legal_principle: A receiver is an officer of the court, and the receiver’s possession cannot be treated as the possession of the successful party with an intention to initiate adverse possession. Limitation cannot begin until the person claiming adverse possession has actual possession and the opposing title-holder is legally able to vindicate that title by action. The court relied on Agency Company v. Short and Dwijendra Narain Roy v. Joges Chandra De, and referred to the principles stated in Kerr on Receivers and Woodroffe on the Law relating to Receivers.

predicates.adverse_possession_claim: A person claims to have acquired title by adverse possession.
predicates.court_receiver_held_property_before_clai: A court-appointed receiver possessed the property before the person claiming adverse possession obtained actual possession.
predicates.claimant_was_initially_out_of_possession: The person claiming adverse possession was not in possession before the receiver took possession.

issues.definition: In an adverse-possession claim, when a court-appointed receiver held the property before an initially dispossessed claimant obtained actual possession, the receiver’s possession is not added to the claimant’s period.

issues.legal_issue: A co-heir’s title is not displaced by adverse possession when the period of the claimant’s actual adverse possession is insufficient, without counting the receiver’s earlier possession.
material_facts: The property was held by a receiver before the person asserting adverse possession obtained actual possession.
The later possessor obtained actual possession from the receiver and thereafter possessed the property.
The suit to recover the co-heir’s share was filed less than twelve years after the later possessor obtained actual possession.
The court assumed, without deciding, that the later possession was adverse and amounted to ouster.
issues.conclusion: The respondent did not lose his title by adverse possession and was entitled to the decree. Even assuming the later possession was adverse, it was insufficient in duration, and the receiver’s possession could not be counted toward it.
issues.legal_principle: Adverse possession must be adequate in continuity, publicity, and extent, and limitation cannot run before the claimant has actual possession under a hostile claim and the opposing party can bring an action to vindicate title. The court relied on Secretary of State for India v. Debendra Lal Khan, Radhamoni Debi v. Collector of Khulna, Agency Company v. Short, and Dwijendra Narain Roy v. Joges Chandra De. No particular provision of the Limitation Act was identified in the judgment as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.coheir_title_displacement_claim: A person seeks to defeat a co-heir’s title by adverse possession.
predicates.claimant_obtained_actual_possession_afte: The person claiming adverse possession obtained actual possession only after a receiver had held the property.
predicates.actual_adverse_possession_period_insuffi: The period of the claimant’s actual adverse possession before the action was insufficient to displace the other co-heir’s title.

issues.definition: A co-heir’s title is not displaced when the claimant obtains actual possession only after a receiver’s possession and the claimant’s own adverse-possession period is insufficient.
